def sweep_supply_chains(
    economy: Economy,
    scenario_template: Scenario,
    *,
    goods: Iterable[str] | None = None,
    target_value: float = 100_000.0,
    keep_results: bool = False,
    tolerance: float = 1e-9,
) -> SupplyChainSweepResult:
    """Analyze every requested good at an equal base-price target value.

    A non-empty ``scenario_template.produce`` basket is ignored with a
    ``UserWarning`` because the sweep generates one normalized target for each
    requested good.
    """
    if scenario_template.produce:
        warnings.warn(
            "scenario_template.produce is ignored; sweep targets are generated "
            "from goods and target_value.",
            UserWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    if not np.isfinite(target_value) or target_value <= 0:
        raise ValueError("target_value must be a positive finite number.")
    selected_goods = list(economy.producible_goods) if goods is None else list(goods)
    if len(selected_goods) != len(set(selected_goods)):
        raise ValueError("goods must not contain duplicates.")
    goods_index = economy.goods_index
    unknown = [good for good in selected_goods if good not in goods_index]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"Goods not found in goods index: {unknown}")

    prices = dict(zip(goods_index, economy.base_prices))
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    retained: dict[str, SupplyChainResult] = {}
    for good in selected_goods:
        price = float(prices[good])
        if not np.isfinite(price) or price <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"Good '{good}' must have a positive finite base price.")
        amount = float(target_value / price)
        name = (
            f"{scenario_template.name}:{good}"
            if scenario_template.name is not None
            else good
        )
        scenario = replace(
            scenario_template,
            produce=((good, amount),),
            name=name,
        )
        try:
            result = SupplyChainAnalyzer(
                economy,
                scenario,
                good,
                tolerance=tolerance,
            ).run()
            row: dict[str, object] = {
                str(key): value for key, value in result.summary().items()
            }
            row.update(
                {
                    "good": good,
                    "status": "success",
                    "error_type": "",
                    "error_message": "",
                }
            )
            if keep_results:
                retained[good] = result
        except ValueError as exc:
            row = {field: float("nan") for field in SUMMARY_FIELDS}
            row.update(
                {
                    "good": good,
                    "status": "failure",
                    "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
                    "error_message": str(exc),
                    "scenario": name,
                    "terminal_good": good,
                    "objective": scenario.objective,
                    "solver_status": -1,
                    "solver_message": str(exc),
                    "target_quantity": amount,
                    "target_base_value": target_value,
                    "terminal_base_price": price,
                }
            )
        rows.append(row)

    summary = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=SWEEP_COLUMNS)
    failures = pd.DataFrame(
        summary.loc[summary["status"].eq("failure"), :]
    ).reset_index(drop=True)
    return SupplyChainSweepResult(
        _summary=summary,
        _failures=failures,
        _results=retained,
    )

docs.title: Data dictionary
docs.text:
This reference covers columns deliberately created, selected, or transformed by the package. It applies to public DataFrame reports and example exports:

  • Parser outputs: identifiers, normalized fields, and generated families.
  • Production configurations: the analytical production table.
  • Economy reports: solved building, market, and population tables and the Japan comparison.
  • Supply-chain reports: summary, detailed reports, sweeps, and example additions.

Arbitrary game-defined attributes copied through unchanged, such as icon in buildings.csv, are outside this dictionary. A patch or mod can introduce such fields without changing the parser. The parser page describes their general representation and the transformations applied to them. Dynamic names with a known meaning are documented once per family, such as goods_<good>; replace the placeholder with the actual script key, for example goods_steel.

docs.title: Shared conventions
docs.text: Convention Interpretation Script identifiers Strings such as building_steel_mills, steel, and pm_bessemer_process; use these for joins. Display translations are separate columns. Configuration identifiers Economy.building_index joins building and the complete production_method string with +. A configuration represents one combination of production methods, not all levels of a building type. Compound strings Many parser lists and production-method combinations use + as a separator. The parser keeps source order; these strings are not localized unless a separate localization column is requested. Numeric types “Number” means integer or floating point as appropriate to source data; solved levels and totals can be fractional because optimization is continuous. CSV has no stored dtype; pandas inference can change with missing values. Goods quantities Weekly goods units or orders, rather than physical SI units. Per-level coefficients describe a fully staffed level; solved totals multiply coefficients by levels and applicable throughput multipliers. Money Game currency (£). Nominal values use goods cost as base price; market values use the state's national prices. Output minus input value excludes payroll and other costs absent from the model. Annualization Annual GDP is weekly GDP multiplied by 52. Employment, building levels, construction points, land, prices, and dimensionless ratios are not annualized. Construction Construction points required to build the modeled levels, not a weekly expense or elapsed construction time. Population / per capita Model totals sum employed workers. These denominators exclude dependents and unemployed population; “per capita” here is per employed person. Fractions and percentages Shares and margins use fractions, so 0.2 means 20%. The economy market report's market_prices_variance instead uses percent units (20 means +20%). Signed infrastructure shares need not lie between zero and one. Infrastructure Positive net usage consumes infrastructure; negative net usage provides it. Zero can mean no footprint or exactly offset consumption and provision. Missing values pd.NA / NaN mean missing or undefined; CSV generally writes them as blank cells. Empty strings also become blank CSV cells and may be read back as NaN. See each table for defaults. Division Production profit ratios use ordinary division: nonzero divided by zero gives signed infinity, and zero divided by zero gives NaN. Supply-chain safe ratios return 0.0 when the denominator is exactly zero; they do not clamp negative denominators. Stable schemas Supply-chain reports retain their named columns even when empty. Generic parser columns depend on the game data; optional enrichments can add or omit columns.

docs.title: Model and source boundaries
docs.text:
The production table aggregates the selected methods' signed goods flows. Economy splits those net coefficients into nonnegative input and output matrices. They are often described as gross input/output matrices in the API, but opposing flows already canceled in a production row cannot be recovered. Profit and GDP measure the modeled goods-value difference, not accounting profit after wages. A process producing multiple goods retains its entire output value; the supply-chain API does not allocate its employment or value added to one coproduct.

Nominal supply-chain optimization uses fixed prices and fixed throughput, without economy-of-scale bonuses. Market solving changes national prices but does not simulate shortages, local prices/MAPI, endogenous population demand, or wealth feedback. Population report wealth starts from the pop-types table; it is not a solved household-income distribution.

Column definitions follow the current source calculations, not a promise that old CSV snapshots match every optional field. See the parsing guide for game-version and localization behavior and the API reference for call signatures.

docs.title: Economy reports
docs.text: These reports export a supplied EconomyState; they do not solve a new scenario. Totals include the entire modeled economy. Monetary values use its state prices, which are base prices in nominal mode and national market prices in market mode. See shared conventions.

docs.title: Building registry
docs.text:
Economy.df_buildings(state) returns one row per configuration with level strictly greater than zero, sorted by level descending. It does not aggregate different configurations of the same building type.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases key String / configuration identifier building + "+" + production_method from Economy.building_index. Not just a building-type key; follows production-row identity. level Float / building levels Solved level for that configuration. Fractional levels are allowed; zero/negative levels are filtered out. construction_cost Float / construction points Per-level construction coefficient times level. Zero-cost configurations can have positive levels.

docs.title: Market report
docs.text:
Economy.df_market(state) returns one row per good with positive sell or buy orders, sorted by sell orders descending. Goods quantities are weekly; they include throughput effects already applied to the state. “Gross” input and output totals are reconstructed from production-table net coefficients.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases goods String / identifier Good key aligned with Economy.goods_index. Includes only goods surviving the order filter. market_prices Float / £ per goods unit Price in the supplied state. Base price in nominal mode; market mode derives it from buy/sell orders. market_prices_variance Float / percent price change 100 * (market_prices / base_prices - 1). 20 means +20%; not statistical variance. Ordinary division at zero base price. sell_orders Float / goods units per week building_goods_output + imports. Zero is valid when only buy orders are positive. buy_orders Float / goods units per week building_goods_input + exports + pop_needs. Zero is valid when only sell orders are positive. building_goods_input Float / goods units per week Sum of configuration levels times adjusted nonnegative input coefficients. Positive consumption magnitude, unlike signed production-table goods columns. building_goods_output Float / goods units per week Sum of configuration levels times adjusted nonnegative output coefficients. Positive production magnitude. imports Float / goods units per week Supplied import orders for the good. Defaults to zero when omitted from solving. exports Float / goods units per week Supplied export orders for the good. Defaults to zero when omitted from solving. pop_needs Float / goods units per week Exogenous population-demand orders supplied to solving. Defaults to zero; not automatically generated from buy-package tables.

docs.title: Population report
docs.text:
Economy.df_pop(state) returns one row per profession with positive employment, sorted by employment descending and with its index reset. Let n_ij be workers of profession j in configuration i, and w_ij their stored wealth level.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases profession String / identifier Profession key aligned with Economy.pop_index. Zero-employment professions are omitted. employment Float / workers sum_i(n_ij). Includes the whole system, not just one terminal chain. employment_share Float / fraction Profession employment divided by all modeled employment. State returns zeros for zero total employment; such a report has no positive-employment rows. avg_wealth Float / wealth level sum_i(w_ij * n_ij) / sum_i(n_ij). State returns zero for a profession without employment. Current solving uses start_quality_of_life from pop types. total_wealth Float / worker-weighted wealth levels sum_i(w_ij * n_ij). Not a stock of money or GDP. pop_balance Float / stored balance total Sum of the state's pop_balance over configurations for this profession. Current nominal and market solvers initialize this array to zero; it is not a computed wage or household budget.

docs.title: Japan optimization comparison
docs.text:
The current examples/optimize_jap.py writes optimize_jap.csv, one row per employment-cap scenario, in increasing cap order. It solves a nominal autarkic era-5 economy with selected Japanese state-region resource and arable-land limits and the example's banned building groups. Its employment and other totals are whole-system values.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases employment_cap Integer / workers Scenario upper bound on total modeled employment. Retained on both success and failure; not the realized employment. status String / category success or failure for the solve. Failure records a caught ValueError. annual_gdp Float / £ per year 52 * state.gdp_weekly, using base prices in this example. NaN on failure. employment Float / workers Sum of the state's employment array. NaN on failure. construction_cost Float / construction points Solved levels dotted with per-level construction coefficients. NaN on failure. gdp_per_capita Float / £ per worker per year Annual GDP divided by modeled employment. Zero for zero employment on a successful state; NaN on failure. arable_land_consumption Float / arable-land units Solved levels dotted with the model's arable-land coefficients. NaN on failure. Recognized agricultural building groups consume one unit per level; others zero. error String / diagnostic text Caught exception message. Empty string on success; no economic metric is inferred from a failure.

docs.title: Additional columns in the committed snapshot
docs.text:
The committed artifacts/analyses/optimization/japan/employment_sweep.csv was generated by an earlier version of the example (the generator at commit 7e3365c used compare_scenarios). It has no status column: an empty error indicates success. Shared metrics have the meanings above, except the earlier per-capita calculation returned infinity when successful employment was zero. These additional columns are still documented for readers of that snapshot; the current generator does not emit them.

Column or family Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases objective String / category Scenario objective, gdp in the Japan snapshot. Snapshot-only; retained on failure. gdp_per_construction Float / £ per year per construction point Annual GDP divided by solved construction cost. Snapshot-only; zero for nonpositive construction cost, NaN on failure. era_cap Integer or None / era limit Scenario's maximum allowed technology era, 5 in this snapshot. Snapshot-only; retained on failure. level_<building> Float / building levels Sum of solved levels across configurations of a resource-limited building type; e.g. level_building_coal_mine. Snapshot-only family in first-seen building order; zero if unbuilt, NaN on failure.

The recognized groups are bg_staple_crops, bg_ranching, bg_agriculture, bg_plantations, bg_subsistence_agriculture, and bg_subsistence_ranching. The coefficient uses immediate building_group membership, not land_usage or ancestor traversal; a missing group column gives all-zero coefficients.

These legacy fields were traced to the earlier comparison implementation; their presence does not imply that the current example and stored snapshot share the same output schema.

For the report APIs, see the economy API. The resource-limited optimization showcase describes the Japan experiment.

docs.title: Parser outputs
docs.text: These entries describe package-defined columns. Other attributes, such as an icon path or an AI weight, are passed through from the game and are not an enumerated schema. Values and concrete family members depend on game version and mods. See shared conventions.

docs.title: Identifiers and localization
docs.text:
Buildings, building groups, goods, population types, state regions, and technologies normally have one row per script definition, identified by key. Population needs instead have one row per need/good entry, so key repeats. Production-method rows use the three identifiers described below. Buy packages use numeric wealth.

Column Type / unit Meaning / source Presence / edge cases key String / identifier Definition key from its source file; in population needs, the need key rather than a unique row key. Included by these parsers, even when other attributes vary. key_localization Nullable string / display text Lookup of key in the requested language. Only with language; missing lookup is pd.NA, with no language fallback. building_localization Nullable string / display text Localized production-method row's building. Only with language on a nonempty production-method table. building_group_localization Nullable string / display text Localized building's building_group. With language if its source column exists. production_method_group_localization Nullable string / display text Localized production-method row's group key. Only with language on a nonempty production-method table. production_method_localization Nullable string / display text Localized production-method row's method key. Only with language on a nonempty production-method table.

Localized text preserves raw game references, formatting, icons, and functions; the parser does not evaluate them. Localization columns are placed beside their identifier. Raw script identifiers remain the join keys.

docs.title: Buildings and building groups
docs.text:
BuildingsParser.to_dataframe() has one row per building. BuildingGroupParser.to_dataframe() has one row per group and does not resolve inheritance. The building export joins the group's resolved scalar attributes. Nested dict/Tree attributes are omitted; lists are +-joined.

Column or family Type / unit Meaning / transformation Presence / edge cases required_construction_points Integer / construction points per level Resolves a building's required_construction script-value name through common/script_values (construction_cost_*). Absent when no reference exists; unknown references warn and skip the value. Other rows can then have NaN in this column. land_usage String / category Joined group value: urban or rural, inherited from the first ancestor that specifies it when missing locally. Unresolved values remain absent/missing; raw group export does not apply inheritance. cash_reserves_max Number / £ per level Joined group cash-reserve ceiling, inherited when missing or zero. An ancestor's zero is also skipped; no reachable value leaves the original value unchanged. economy_of_scale Boolean / flag Joined group eligibility, inherited when missing from the child group. Explicit false is retained; the production table additionally excludes subsistence buildings. building_group_<attribute> Source-dependent / inherited source unit Collision-prefixed joined group attribute when its name already exists in the building row. For example, building_group_land_usage. Collision handling is per row; the concrete attributes are game-defined. Building values are preserved.

Other joined scalar group attributes remain group-local rather than inherited. Parent-chain traversal stops at unknown parents or cycles. A missing group reference warns and skips the join. These are transformations, not a claim that every named field exists in every input definition.

docs.title: Production methods
docs.text:
ProductionMethodParser.to_dataframe() has one row per building/production-method-group/production-method membership, not one row per complete building configuration. The same method can occur in multiple rows. Scalar method attributes are passed through, lists are +-joined, and nested containers are omitted. The computed families below are zero-filled.

Column or family Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases building String / identifier Building whose production-method group contains this method. Fixed row identifier. production_method_group String / identifier Group providing the method choice. Fixed row identifier; unknown referenced groups raise an error. production_method String / identifier Single chosen method in that group. Fixed row identifier; complete combinations are formed by production_table(). employment Number / workers per level Sum of building_employment_* values in the method's level_scaled building modifiers. Zero when absent; negative automation adjustments are retained. employment_<profession> Number / workers per level Value of building_employment_<profession>_add; e.g. employment_laborers. Family discovered from employment modifiers; absent method/profession values are zero. goods_<good> Number / goods units per week per level Signed workforce_scaled goods modifier: output positive, input negative; e.g. goods_tools. Accepts goods_(output\|input)_<good>_add and legacy building_(output\|input)_<good>_add names. One column per supplied/parsed good; absent flows zero. The parser assigns matched modifiers rather than resolving arbitrary game effects.

State-modifier keys are also flattened from unscaled, level_scaled, and workforce_scaled blocks and zero-filled across rows. Their concrete names and units are game-defined and excluded from the enumerated dictionary. Flattening drops the scaling-block distinction; duplicate keys across blocks of a method raise ValueError. One explicitly consumed modifier, state_infrastructure_add, represents infrastructure generation in the production table's net-footprint calculation; it is present in the method table only if discovered in the inputs.

docs.title: Technologies
docs.text:
One row per technology. Nested dict/Tree blocks are omitted and lists are +-joined; remaining scalar attributes are passed through.

Column Type / unit Meaning / transformation Presence / edge cases era Integer / era number Converts source era_N to numeric N. Converted when present; an unparsable era raises ValueError. The parser does not synthesize a missing era.

docs.title: Population needs
docs.text:
PopNeedsParser.to_dataframe() emits one row per need/good substitution entry. Rows are identified by the need key and eligible good. These six columns remain present in an empty result; localization is optional.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases key String / identifier Population need to which the entry belongs. Repeats across eligible goods. goods String / identifier Good allowed to satisfy the need, from the entry's goods. Missing entry field remains missing. weight Number / relative weight Base substitution weight applied to the good based on market sell-order share, preserved without normalization. Defaults to 1 when absent. max_supply_share Number / fraction Sell-order share ceiling above which additional relative supply no longer increases the applied base weight. Defaults to 1; stored rather than enforced by the parser. min_supply_share Number / fraction Minimum multiplier of base weight applied regardless of the good's sell-order share. Defaults to 0; stored rather than enforced by the parser. is_default Boolean / flag Whether the entry's good equals the need's default good. Computed by equality; a need without entries raises an error.

docs.title: Buy packages
docs.text:
buy_packages() emits one row per matching wealth_N definition, sorted by numeric wealth. popneed_* entries represent population needs, not individual tradeable goods. Game buy packages express base-value budgets for 10,000 working adults. The values below retain those source amounts, not converted physical goods quantities or realized demand from Economy.

Column or family Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases wealth Integer / wealth level Numeric N extracted from the wealth_N key. Nonmatching definitions are skipped. political_strength Number / source political-strength factor The wealth definition's political_strength. Missing source value remains missing; not included in the needs total. total_popneeds Number / £ base-value budget per 10,000 working adults Sum of all popneed_* values in this wealth row. Zero when no matching needs exist; no population scaling is performed. popneed_<need> Number / £ base-value budget per 10,000 working adults Need amount from the definition's goods block; e.g. popneed_basic_food. Columns follow first-seen order; absence at a wealth level is zero-filled.

docs.title: State regions
docs.text:
One row per state region. Arbitrary scalar attributes are passed through; nested attributes and province/trait/arable-resource lists are omitted, apart from the transformations below.

Column or family Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases province_count Integer / provinces Counts all provinces entries in the parsed region tree. Zero when none are found; does not subtract impassable provinces. resource_<building> Integer / potential building levels Capacity from capped_resources, or undiscovered_amount + discovered_amount from a resource block. Example: resource_building_oil_rig. Only encountered resource types become columns; missing/non-numeric cells are coerced to zero and converted to integers. undiscovered_amount_resource_<building> Integer / building levels Undiscovered component of a resource block. Defaults to zero within the block; exists only for encountered resource-block types. discovered_amount_resource_<building> Integer / building levels Discovered component of a resource block. Defaults to zero within the block; not synthesized for capped-resource entries.

These capacities describe definitions, not a save game's current discoveries or exploitation. state_region_resource_limits() uses total-potential resource_* columns only. It sums selected regions once each, treats missing/non-numeric values as zero, adds gold-field potential to gold-mine capacity, and sets gold-field capacity to zero. The separate arable-land helper sums the source arable_land field; that raw attribute is not synthesized by the parser.

docs.title: Goods and population types
docs.text:
Beyond the shared key and optional key_localization, these tables preserve game-defined attributes and do not add analytical columns. Population types omit nested containers and +-join lists. Goods preserve the source attribute values directly, including any nested values. The model consumes goods cost as base price and population-type start_quality_of_life, wage_weight, and paid_private_wage; their role in derived metrics is documented on the production and economy pages.

See the parsing API for constructors and source directories.

docs.title: Production configurations
docs.text: production_table() and production_table.csv contain one row per enumerated building configuration: one method from each of the building's method groups. The building and complete production_method string identify the row. The table does not filter combinations by a particular scenario or all gameplay conditions. Values describe one fully staffed building level, before throughput bonuses, and use goods base prices. See shared conventions.

docs.title: Identity, metadata, and requirements
docs.text: Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases building String / identifier Source building key. Always included. building_localization Nullable string / display text Building label propagated from the buildings input. Only if its input localization column exists; unknown labels are pd.NA. production_method String / identifiers Selected method keys joined by +, in building method-group order. Always included; identifies a complete combination. production_method_localization Nullable string / display text Selected method labels joined by +. Only if method localization input exists; any missing label makes the whole result pd.NA. building_group String / identifier Building's immediate group. Always included from buildings input. building_group_localization Nullable string / display text Propagated label for that group. Only with the buildings input's group localization column. parent_group Nullable string / identifier Parent group metadata joined onto the source building. Defaults to pd.NA when the source column is absent; not the entire ancestor chain. land_usage Nullable string / category Source building's resolved land-use category. Defaults to pd.NA if absent; see parser inheritance rules. is_subsistence Boolean / flag Source subsistence-building flag. Missing values/column become false. discoverable_resource Boolean / flag Source discoverable-resource flag. Missing values/column become false; not a numerical resource cap. depletable_resource Boolean / flag Source depletable-resource flag. Missing values/column become false; no depletion is simulated. economy_of_scale Boolean / eligibility flag Source economy_of_scale is true and source is_subsistence is false. Missing flags become false; eligibility does not apply a throughput bonus to this table. urbanization Number / urbanization points per level Source building's urbanization contribution. Missing value becomes zero. infrastructure_usage_per_level Number / infrastructure points per level Source infrastructure usage minus the sum of chosen methods' state_infrastructure_add. Missing usage becomes zero; absent modifier column warns and is zero-filled. Negative means provision. era Integer / era number Maximum era of the building's and chosen methods' unlocking technologies. Only with df_tech; zero if no required technologies; unknown required technologies raise an error. unlocking_tech String / identifiers Building requirements followed by chosen method requirements, deduplicated in first-seen order and joined by +. Always included; empty string for no requirements. unlocking_tech_localization Nullable string / display text Required technology labels joined by +. Only with a localized technology input; empty requirements or any missing label yield pd.NA. construction_cost Integer / construction points per level Building's resolved required_construction_points. Missing cost becomes zero; construction cost is not subtracted from weekly profit.

docs.title: Employment and goods flows
docs.text:
Column or family Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases employment Number / workers per level Sum of chosen methods' total employment. Always included; includes automation adjustments. employment_<profession> Number / workers per level Sum of chosen methods' profession-specific employment; e.g. employment_engineers. One column per profession present in the methods input. wage_normalized_employment Number / private-wage-equivalent workers per level Sum of profession employment times wage_weight, counting only professions whose paid_private_wage flag is true. Only with df_pop_types; missing private-wage flags default to true, including when the column is absent in older game data. Invalid or missing required profession weights raise an error. goods_<good> Number / goods units per week per level Sum of the chosen methods' signed flow for the good: positive output, negative input. One per goods-table key, in goods-table row order; missing methods input columns warn and are zero-filled. Unpriced goods columns are ignored with a warning. input_ratio_goods_<good> Float / fraction max(-goods_<good>, 0) / sum(max(-goods_<all goods>, 0)). Immediately follows its goods column. Zero for outputs, zero flows, and configurations without net inputs.

The input ratios use physical net-input quantities, not base-value shares. They sum to one when net inputs exist, otherwise zero. They cannot recover inputs offset by outputs of the same good. Prestige variants share the base good's column. Victoria 3's prestige-goods throughput bonus uses gross input base value; multiplying these ratios by the game's 20% maximum gives only a quantity-based analytical proxy.

For example, net inputs of 10 tools and 30 coal have quantity shares 0.25 and 0.75 regardless of their different prices. A net output contributes zero.

docs.title: Nominal economic metrics
docs.text:
Let q_g be the row's signed goods flow, p_g the goods base price, I = sum(max(-q_g, 0) * p_g), and O = sum(max(q_g, 0) * p_g). Let L be employment, W wage-normalized employment, and C construction cost. These input/output valuations split net flows; payroll is not subtracted. All monetary flows are weekly.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases value_goods_inputs_nominal Float / £ per week per level I: base-price value of negative net goods flows. Zero when no net inputs. value_goods_outputs_nominal Float / £ per week per level O: base-price value of positive net goods flows. Zero when no net outputs. profit_nominal Float / £ per week per level O - I, modeled goods-value surplus. Can be negative; excludes wages and construction expenditure. profit_margin_nominal Float / fraction (O - I) / O. Ordinary division; negative infinity if output value is zero and profit is negative, NaN for zero/zero. profit_per_capita_nominal Float / £ per worker per week (O - I) / L. Per employed worker; zero denominator can yield signed infinity or NaN. profit_per_wage_normalized_employment_nominal Float / £ per wage-equivalent worker per week (O - I) / W. Only with df_pop_types; ordinary division, with no payroll subtraction. profit_per_construction_cost_nominal Float / £ per week per construction point (O - I) / C. Ordinary division; zero construction cost can yield signed infinity or NaN.

Weekly profit and the per-worker/per-construction profit rates can be multiplied by 52 for annual equivalents. Do not annualize profit_margin_nominal or input shares. Missing localized text and undefined numeric ratios can both appear as blank CSV cells, but have different meanings.

See the economy and production API and parsing guide.

docs.title: Supply-chain reports
docs.text: SupplyChainAnalyzer solves a nominal scenario for exactly one positive target good. Its immutable result exposes the reports below. All schemas remain present when a report is empty. See shared conventions and the supply-chain guide.

docs.title: Scope, prices, and graph views
docs.text:
• System means every configuration in the solved state, including any production outside the terminal good's upstream chain.
  • Chain means processes in the realized terminal graph: active upstream producers, with their input goods and all coproduct outputs retained. Each included process contributes its whole employment, cost, and value added; nothing is allocated to individual coproducts.
  • realized graphs start from configurations whose level exceeds tolerance (default 1e-9). allowed graphs start from configurations not disabled by the era cap, PM bans, exact building-group bans, or building limits at or below tolerance. Both are restricted to the terminal's upstream graph and attached coproducts. Allowed membership does not prove LP feasibility.
  • processes(view), goods(view), and flows(view) use the requested graph, defaulting to realized. Even in allowed, quantities use the same solved levels; inactive alternatives do not get hypothetical production.
  • Input/output coefficients include the compiled fixed throughput multiplier. It scales goods, not employment, construction, land, or infrastructure. Coefficients split production-table net flows into positive input/output magnitudes; flows already offset in that table cannot be recovered.
  • Prices are state prices: base prices for the public nominal analyzer. The market automobile example at the end of this page has a separate schema.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
result.summary() is a Series with these fixed fields, named after the terminal good. Sweeps turn them into columns. On a successful analyzer result, all fields are present. Let Q denote whole-system terminal net output, G_chain chain weekly value added, and L_chain chain employment. Safe division returns zero only for an exactly zero denominator.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases scenario String / label Scenario.display_name(). Uses explicit scenario name or the generated display name. terminal_good String / identifier The single good being analyzed. Matches the scenario's production target. objective String / category Nominal objective: gdp, employment, automation, or construction_cost. gdp_per_capita is rejected by the analyzer. solver_status Integer / status code HiGHS result status. Successful solves normally report 0; sweep failures use synthetic -1. solver_message String / diagnostic text HiGHS message retained from the solve. Sweep failures instead retain the exception message. objective_value Float / objective units Whole-system attained objective: weekly GDP (£/week), employment (workers), automation (workers), or construction points. Sign restored for maximized GDP/employment; not necessarily a chain-only metric. target_quantity Float / goods units per week Requested production target. Strictly positive; a lower bound on net production, not realized gross output. target_base_value Float / £ per week Target quantity times terminal state price. Equals base value in nominal analysis; sweep preserves requested value on failure. terminal_base_price Float / £ per goods unit Terminal price from the state. Base price in nominal analysis; not an annual rate. terminal_gross_output Float / goods units per week Whole-system terminal building_goods_output. Before subtracting terminal consumption by processes. terminal_net_output Float / goods units per week Q = levels @ net_matrix[:, terminal]. Whole-system output minus process inputs; not reduced by exports or population orders. terminal_surplus Float / goods units per week terminal_net_output - target_quantity. Can be slightly negative within solver tolerance; not a market order balance. system_gdp_weekly Float / £ per week Sum of system output minus input quantities valued at state prices. Excludes payroll; imports/exports are not separately added to GDP. system_gdp_annual Float / £ per year 52 * system_gdp_weekly. Annualization only, not a second solve. chain_gdp_weekly Float / £ per week G_chain = sum(realized process value_added). Includes entire coproduct values of included processes. chain_gdp_annual Float / £ per year 52 * chain_gdp_weekly. Same process scope as weekly chain GDP. system_employment Float / workers Sum of all state employment. Model population means employed workers. chain_employment Float / workers L_chain = sum(realized process employment). No allocation to individual output goods. system_construction_cost Float / construction points Whole-system levels dotted with construction coefficients. A stock of required construction, not a weekly cost. chain_construction_cost Float / construction points Sum of realized process construction costs. Can be zero for zero-cost configurations. system_arable_land Float / arable-land units Whole-system levels dotted with land coefficients. Uses the immediate agricultural group rule on the economy dictionary page. chain_arable_land Float / arable-land units Sum of realized process arable land. Zero when no included process consumes modeled arable land. system_net_infrastructure_usage Float / infrastructure points Whole-system levels dotted with net infrastructure coefficients. Negative means net infrastructure provision. chain_net_infrastructure_usage Float / infrastructure points Sum of realized process net infrastructure usage. Also signed; not an absolute consumption total. employment_per_terminal_unit Float / workers per unit/week of output capacity L_chain / Q. Safe division; denominator is net system output, not the target or gross output. construction_per_terminal_unit Float / construction points per unit/week of output capacity chain_construction_cost / Q. Safe division; construction is not annualized. gdp_per_terminal_unit Float / £ per terminal goods unit G_chain / Q. Both GDP and net production are weekly; their time factors cancel. output_per_10k_workers Float / goods units per week per 10,000 workers Q * 10000 / L_chain. Safe division; zero if chain employment is exactly zero. realized_process_count Integer / nodes Number of configurations in the realized graph. Counts configurations, not summed building levels. realized_good_count Integer / nodes Number of good nodes in the realized graph. Includes terminal and attached coproduct goods. realized_edge_count Integer / edges Number of directed goods/process edges in the realized graph. Input and output edges count separately. allowed_process_count Integer / nodes Number of configurations in the allowed graph. Includes inactive alternatives upstream of the terminal. allowed_good_count Integer / nodes Number of good nodes in the allowed graph. Does not count every good in the economy. allowed_edge_count Integer / edges Number of directed edges in the allowed graph. Not the number of diagram edges after visualization pruning. cyclic_component_count Integer / components Realized strongly connected components with more than one node, or a self-loop. Zero for an acyclic graph. cyclic_node_count Integer / nodes Number of realized nodes participating in a directed cycle. Counts both goods and process nodes. condensation_depth Integer / edges Longest directed-path length after each realized strongly connected component becomes one node. Zero for an empty or single-component condensation; counts bipartite graph edges. extractive_process_count Integer / configurations Count of realized processes marked is_extractive. Uses immediate parent bg_extraction or either resource flag. resource_process_count Integer / configurations Count with discoverable_resource or depletable_resource. A process with both flags counts once; not resource capacity or remaining stock. chain_gdp_share Float / signed ratio chain_gdp_weekly / system_gdp_weekly. Safe division; negative or offsetting contributions can put the ratio outside [0, 1]. chain_employment_share Float / fraction chain_employment / system_employment. Safe division. chain_construction_share Float / fraction chain_construction_cost / system_construction_cost. Safe division. chain_arable_land_share Float / fraction chain_arable_land / system_arable_land. Safe division. chain_infrastructure_share Float / signed ratio chain_net_infrastructure_usage / system_net_infrastructure_usage. Safe division; cancellation and negative values mean it need not lie in [0, 1].

Graph counts use the complete retained graphs. They are independent of the top-producer pruning used by a plotted or Mermaid allowed view.

docs.title: Processes
docs.text:
result.processes(view) has one row per configuration in the requested graph, in production-table row order. Let x be its solved level, m its throughput multiplier, I its adjusted input value per level, and O its adjusted output value per level. Unit economics retain all output goods.

Here, process means a building with its complete PM combination, rather than the building type alone. The guide explains the naming rationale and parallels with Brightway.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases config String / configuration identifier Economy.building_index key for the row. Joins to flows.process and workforce/alternatives config. building String / identifier Source building key. Multiple configurations may share it. production_method String / compound identifiers Complete chosen method combination. Methods are joined by +. building_group String / identifier Immediate source building group. Missing metadata defaults to empty string. parent_group String / identifier Immediate parent metadata of that group. Missing metadata defaults to empty string. land_usage String / category Source resolved land-use metadata. Missing metadata defaults to empty string; not the land coefficient itself. era Integer / era number Source configuration era. Required by the reporting implementation. allowed Boolean / membership flag Process node is in the terminal's allowed graph. Graph membership, not independent LP feasibility. active Boolean / solved flag x > tolerance. May be false in the allowed view. in_terminal_chain Boolean / membership flag Configuration appears in the realized terminal graph. An active process elsewhere in the system can still be false. level Float / building levels x, from the whole solved state. Fractional or zero levels are valid. throughput_multiplier Float / multiplier Compiled fixed goods multiplier m. 1 means unchanged; excludes level-dependent economy of scale. unit_input_cost Float / £ per week per level I = adjusted input row @ state prices. Includes throughput; zero with no modeled inputs. unit_output_value Float / £ per week per level O = adjusted output row @ state prices. Includes every coproduct. unit_value_added Float / £ per week per level O - I. Can be negative; excludes wages. input_cost Float / £ per week I * x. Zero for a zero-level allowed alternative. output_value Float / £ per week O * x. Zero for a zero-level allowed alternative. value_added Float / £ per week (O - I) * x. Entire process contribution, not allocated to one good. employment Float / workers Per-level employment coefficient times x. Not multiplied by m. construction_cost Float / construction points Per-level construction coefficient times x. Not multiplied by m. arable_land Float / arable-land units Per-level land coefficient times x. Uses immediate group membership; not multiplied by m. net_infrastructure_usage Float / infrastructure points Per-level net infrastructure coefficient times x. Signed; not multiplied by m. is_extractive Boolean / classification flag Immediate parent_group == "bg_extraction" or either resource flag in allowed-graph metadata. Defaults false if no matching metadata; does not traverse ancestors. is_subsistence Boolean / source flag Source subsistence metadata. Missing metadata defaults false. discoverable_resource Boolean / source flag Source discoverable-resource metadata. Missing metadata defaults false. depletable_resource Boolean / source flag Source depletable-resource metadata. Missing metadata defaults false; depletion is not simulated.

docs.title: Goods
docs.text:
result.goods(view) has one row per good node in the requested graph, in economy goods order. Production and consumption sum only processes in that view, while imports, exports, and population orders come from the whole state. This mix of scopes means these balances need not equal whole-system market balances. Producer counts use the two retained graphs irrespective of the requested view.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases good String / identifier Good key. Includes attached coproduct goods. terminal Boolean / flag Whether this is the analyzed terminal good. True only for the terminal key. price Float / £ per goods unit State price for this good. Base price in nominal analysis. production Float / goods units per week View-process levels times adjusted output coefficients. Zero is valid for an input-only good or inactive allowed production. consumption Float / goods units per week View-process levels times adjusted input coefficients. Positive magnitude, not a negative signed flow. imports Float / goods units per week Whole-state imported orders. Zero when no imports supplied. exports Float / goods units per week Whole-state exported orders. Zero when no exports supplied. pop_needs Float / goods units per week Whole-state exogenous population orders. Zero when no population orders supplied. sell_orders Float / goods units per week View production + imports. Combines view and state scope. buy_orders Float / goods units per week View consumption + exports + pop_needs. Combines view and state scope. net_balance Float / goods units per week sell_orders - buy_orders. Signed; differs from terminal net production. output_value Float / £ per week View production * price. Imports are not included. input_value Float / £ per week View consumption * price. Exports/population orders are not included. input_cost_share Float / fraction input_value / total input value of all view processes. Safe division; zero when total input value is zero. allowed_producers Integer / configurations Process predecessors of this good in the allowed graph. Restricted graph count, not every producer in the economy. active_producers Integer / configurations Process predecessors of this good in the realized graph. Count unaffected by view; does not sum their levels.

docs.title: Flows
docs.text:
result.flows(view) has one row per directed graph edge, sorted by the source and target node strings. Inputs point from goods to processes; outputs point from processes to goods. Rates and amounts are positive magnitudes.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases source String / node identifier Edge source: good:<key> or process:<config>. Direction depends on role. target String / node identifier Edge target: process:<config> or good:<key>. Direction depends on role. role String / category input or output. Distinguishes flow direction without a signed rate. good String / identifier Good carried by this edge. Same key as the goods report. process String / configuration identifier Configuration key, without the process: prefix. Same key as process config. unit_rate Float / goods units per week per level Adjusted input or output coefficient. Includes throughput; edges are created only for coefficients > 0. realized_amount Float / goods units per week unit_rate * solved process level. Can be zero for an allowed alternative. price Float / £ per goods unit State price for the edge's good. Base price in nominal analysis. realized_value Float / £ per week realized_amount * price. Zero for an inactive flow. active Boolean / flow flag realized_amount > tolerance. Amount threshold, distinct from process level threshold. in_cycle Boolean / endpoint flag Both endpoints are cyclic nodes in the requested graph. Does not require them to belong to the same cyclic component; do not interpret it as an exact cycle-edge test.

docs.title: Workforce
docs.text:
result.workforce() uses only realized-chain configurations, in row order then profession order. It omits process/profession employment at or below tolerance.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases config String / configuration identifier Configuration employing the profession. Joins to processes. building String / identifier Configuration's source building. Multiple rows can share it. profession String / identifier Profession key from the economy's profession index. No row for employment at or below tolerance. employment Float / workers State employment cell for this configuration/profession. Per-level profession coefficient times solved level; throughput does not change it.

docs.title: Constraints and bottlenecks
docs.text:
result.constraints() exposes compiled LP rows, inequalities first and equalities second, in their named slice order. Constraints apply to the whole system. Inequalities are stored in canonical form A_ub @ levels <= b_ub; for example a minimum production target is stored with negative coefficients and a negative bound. Interpret the compiled sign before converting a marginal to a gameplay change. Variable bounds are not rows in this report.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases kind String / category inequality or equality. Determines slack/residual interpretation. family String / constraint identifier Named compiled constraint slice, such as produce, import_limit, or building_limits. Only families present in the compiled problem appear. label String / row label Good/building/group key for applicable families; PM bans use their +-joined keys; other rows use the family name. If label count differs from row count, uses family[i]. realized_value Float / compiled row units A_row @ solved levels. Signed canonical left-hand side, not always the physical quantity named by the family. bound Float / compiled row units Stored right-hand side b_row. A lower-bound target can be represented as a negative bound. slack Float / compiled row units For inequalities, bound - realized_value. NaN for equalities; slightly negative values can occur within solver tolerance. residual Float / compiled row units For equalities, realized_value - bound. Exactly 0 in this column for inequalities. binding Boolean / threshold flag Inequality slack <= tolerance; equality abs(residual) <= tolerance. Numerical criterion, not proof that relaxing the row improves the objective. solver_marginal Float / solver objective units per compiled bound unit Raw HiGHS derivative of its minimized objective with respect to this right-hand side. NaN if diagnostics unavailable; GDP/employment objectives are negated for minimization. improvement_per_unit Float / solver objective units per compiled bound unit For a finite inequality marginal, max(0, -solver_marginal). NaN for equalities or unavailable/nonfinite marginals; local sensitivity to increasing the canonical bound.

For minimized construction/automation, positive improvement means lowering the minimized cost. For maximized GDP/employment, it means increasing the reported objective. It measures one unit of the compiled RHS, so relaxing a negative production constraint means lowering its requested physical minimum. It is local LP sensitivity and is not a guaranteed finite-change benefit.

result.bottlenecks() returns the same columns, restricted to binding inequalities with improvement_per_unit > tolerance, sorted by improvement descending, then family and label. It has no separate schema.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
result.alternatives(good) lists producer predecessors of the specified good in the terminal's allowed graph. With no argument it covers all goods in that graph. It sorts by good, selected first, unit output descending, then config. Unit costs and values describe the entire process, not only the requested good. “Selected” means membership in the realized chain, not simply a positive level anywhere in the system.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases good String / identifier Good for which this process is an alternative producer. A coproduct process can appear once per output good. config String / configuration identifier Allowed producer configuration key. No row if the good has no producer in the allowed graph. building String / identifier Source building key. Same metadata as the process report. production_method String / compound identifiers Complete method combination. +-joined. era Integer / era number Configuration's required era. Same metadata as the process report. unit_output Float / goods units per week per level Adjusted output coefficient for this good. Includes throughput, unlike the all-goods monetary unit fields. unit_input_cost Float / £ per week per level Whole adjusted process input row valued at state prices. Includes all process inputs. unit_output_value Float / £ per week per level Whole adjusted process output row valued at state prices. Includes every coproduct. unit_value_added Float / £ per week per level unit_output_value - unit_input_cost. Excludes wages; can be negative. selected Boolean / membership flag Configuration occurs in the realized terminal graph. False for alternatives outside that chain, even if active elsewhere. level Float / building levels Whole-state solved level of the configuration. Zero allowed for an inactive alternative. parent_group String / identifier Parent metadata from the allowed graph. Missing metadata defaults to empty string. land_usage String / category Land-use metadata from the allowed graph. Missing metadata defaults to empty string. is_extractive Boolean / classification flag Immediate parent bg_extraction or either resource flag. No ancestor traversal. is_subsistence Boolean / source flag Source subsistence flag. Missing metadata defaults false. discoverable_resource Boolean / source flag Source discoverable-resource flag. Missing metadata defaults false. depletable_resource Boolean / source flag Source depletable-resource flag. Missing metadata defaults false.

docs.title: Sweep summary and failures
docs.text:
sweep_supply_chains() generates one scenario per requested good, preserving the requested order (by default economy.producible_goods order). Each quantity is target_value / base_price; every requested base price must be finite and positive. sweep.summary contains these fields followed by all summary fields. sweep.failures is the failed subset with the same columns and a reset index, including when empty.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases good String / identifier Good selected for this sweep row. Matches terminal_good; retained on failures. status String / category success or failure. Failed solves do not stop subsequent goods. error_type String / exception name Type of caught analysis exception. Empty on success; currently ValueError on recorded failures. error_message String / diagnostic text Caught exception message. Empty on success; retained on failure.

On failure, scenario, terminal good, objective, target quantity, requested base value, and terminal base price remain populated. solver_status becomes -1 and solver_message becomes the exception text. All remaining summary fields are NaN, including counts and objective_value; they do not mean zero. Sweep input-validation errors raise before an applicable result rather than becoming failure rows. A template's produce basket is ignored with a warning.

docs.title: Example CSV additions
docs.text:
The nominal example exports retain every sweep field, including its failure policy, and add these labels. The comparison summary.csv has one row per configuration/good pair; video summary.csv files have one row per variant/good pair. Detailed results live under analyses/supply_chains/<configuration>/<good>/; cross-good summary.csv files live at configuration level. Cross-configuration comparisons live under analyses/supply_chains/comparison/summary.csv, alongside the population, construction, and annual GDP per capita charts pop.svg, construction_points.svg, and gdp_per_capita.svg. Labels describe presets, not additional economic metrics.

Column Type / unit Meaning / source Presence / edge cases configuration String / preset label Scenario preset in examples/supply_chain_compare.py. In comparison and preset summary CSVs; rows retain it on failure. variant String / preset label base or a named product-specific variant in examples/supply_chain_cangshulun.py. Only in video summary CSVs; base covers all producible goods, named variants selected goods. ban_config String / preset label Ban-policy label supplied by the example. Retained on failure; an empty label in the comparison export does not mean no default building-group bans. system_gdp_per_capita_annual Float / £ per worker per year system_gdp_annual / system_employment. Only in comparison and preset summary CSVs; zero for successful solves with zero employment, NaN on failure.

docs.text: See the production-table dictionary for input coefficients and the economy-report dictionary for exported state columns, formulas, and units.

docs.title: Economy data and alignment
docs.text:
It takes three kinds of information to define an Economy model: production table, goods table, and pop types table, each of which being presented by a parsed DataFrame in parsing.

You can either construct an Economy from the parsed tables, or let it parse them internally as below:

from vic3_analysis import Economy
economy = Economy()

Immutability

Economy is a frozen dataclass that deep-copies its input tables. Its public DataFrames remain mutable, but editing them is unsupported: construct a new Economy for changed model data, because cached coefficients are not invalidated. Indexes (building_index, goods_index, pop_index, and producible_goods) are cached tuples. Fixed coefficients such as base_prices, employment_matrix, employment_vector, construction_cost_vector, arable_land_vector, infrastructure_vector, and pop_wealth_init are cached, read-only arrays.

To display names while keeping the model's key-based alignment, request a language when parsing the internal tables:

from vic3_analysis import Economy

economy = Economy(language="english")

Localization is added only to internally parsed DataFrames. If df_production, df_goods, or df_pop_types is supplied explicitly, its contents are copied without adding localization or changing the supplied data.

import numpy as np

unscaled = economy.goods_input_matrix_unscaled
multipliers = np.full(unscaled.shape[0], 2.0)
scaled = economy.goods_input_matrix(throughput_multipliers=multipliers)

docs.title: Direct solving
docs.text:
Now that we have a model of the economy, if we know the levels of each building, we can solve for all kinds of metrics we care about, such as employment, goods flows, and GDP, all of which stored in the EconomyState dataclass.

import numpy as np
# Assume we have one level of everything
levels = np.ones(len(economy.building_index), dtype=np.float64)
state = economy.solve(levels)
print("Class of the state:", type(state))
print("Annual GDP: ", state.gdp(annual=True))
print("Total employed population: ", state.total_population)

Economy.solve() default to nominal mode, which ignores the market price mechanic and uses base prices for each good.

You can also use market mode, which derives national prices from buy and sell orders, just like the game does (still no local prices though).

Economy.solve() also supports throughput bonuses via economy of scale and parameterized throughput_multipliers. The two are applied additively to the raw throughput of each building, which is then used to compute goods flows.

Set economy_of_scale_level_cap=20.0 to apply up to +20% economy of scale throughput; leave it at 0.0 to disable the effect.

import numpy as np

levels = np.ones(len(economy.building_index), dtype=np.float64)
state = economy.solve(
    levels,
    method="market",
    throughput_multipliers=np.full(len(economy.building_index), 1.5),
    economy_of_scale_level_cap=20.0
)

To choose building levels from objectives and constraints, continue with the optimization guide. See the economy API for model parameters and state reports.

docs.title: Optimization
docs.text:
Mathematical Programming is the foundation of analyzing and optimizing Victoria 3's economy. The vic3_analysis package provides optimizers that choose building levels, which maximize or minimize the objective, for an Economy according to a scenario's constraints. Start with an economy model:

from vic3_analysis import Economy

economy = Economy()

See the economy guide for model construction and direct solving, and the economy-report dictionary for returned state columns, formulas, and units.

docs.title: Scenario definition
docs.text:
Objective and constraints are defined in an immutable Scenario dataclass. Create a new scenario to change its assumptions.

  • Use game script keys when setting attributes of Scenario, such as "steel" or "building_steel_mills", rather than localized display names.
  • Fields containing pairs use tuples such as (("steel", 100.0),)
  • Fields containing only keys use tuples such as ("pm_diesel_engines",).
  • An empty tuple () adds no entries.
  • Optional caps default to None, which leaves that constraint disabled.
  • The decision variables are non-negative, continuous (Fractional levels are allowed) building levels for each production configuration.
  • Use weekly flows when setting goods quantities
  • Employment is the workforce headcount, excluding dependents.

docs.title: Scenario name
docs.text: Attribute Default Meaning name None Optional label for the experiment; it does not affect the solution. display_name() returns this label, otherwise joins the produce good keys with +, or returns "unnamed" when there are no targets.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
The objective attribute defaults to "automation". Its supported values are:

Objective Direction Meaning Optimizer gdp maximize Model GDP: net goods output valued at base prices with NominalOptimizer, or endogenous market prices with MarketOptimizer. Both gdp_per_capita maximize Market-price GDP divided by employed population. Market only employment maximize Total employed population. Nominal only automation minimize Employment required to satisfy the constraints. Nominal only construction_cost minimize Total construction cost required to satisfy the constraints. Nominal only

docs.title: Production targets and market orders
docs.text:
Attribute Default Meaning produce () (good, amount) pairs setting minimum weekly net domestic output after production inputs are deducted. For example, (("steel", 100.0),) requires at least 100 steel per week. Each target is a separate constraint; imports do not satisfy it. import_limit 0.0 Maximum weekly net production deficit per good, using the same cap for every good. 0.0 enforces autarkic production balance; 10.0 allows each good's net domestic output to fall as low as −10. None disables these balance constraints and is required by MarketOptimizer. This field does not set fixed import orders. imports () Fixed (good, amount) weekly import orders, added to market sell orders. With MarketOptimizer, they affect prices. They are separate from import_limit and are not optimized. exports () Fixed (good, amount) weekly export orders, added to market buy orders. With MarketOptimizer, they affect prices. Add a produce target separately when domestic production must cover an export quantity. pop_needs () Fixed (good, amount) weekly population-consumption orders, added to market buy orders. Supply quantities by good, such as (("grain", 200.0),), rather than pop-need category keys. These orders do not enforce a domestic production requirement.

imports, exports, and pop_needs require known good keys and finite, non-negative amounts; repeated entries for the same good are summed. They do not alter the nominal optimizer's objective or constraints, but are passed to the returned economy state. The market optimizer uses them to calculate prices, without requiring buy and sell orders to balance.

docs.title: Available configurations and throughput
docs.text:
Attribute Default Meaning banned_pms () Production-method keys to exclude. Every production configuration containing any listed method is forced to zero levels. banned_building_groups () Building-group keys to exclude. Configurations whose building_group exactly matches a listed key are forced to zero; parent-group descendants are not matched automatically. era_cap None Highest permitted technology era. Configurations whose production-table era exceeds this value are forced to zero levels. Requires an era-enriched production table. throughput_bonuses () (building, multiplier) pairs applied to every configuration of that building. Despite the attribute name, 1.5 means 150% throughput (+50%), not a +150% bonus. Gross goods inputs and outputs both scale; employment and construction cost per level do not. Repeated entries for one building multiply together.

Both optimizers disable level-dependent economy-of-scale bonuses. Use fixed throughput_bonuses to represent throughput assumptions in the scenario.

docs.title: Capacity and relationship constraints
docs.text: Attribute Default Meaning building_limits () (building, maximum_levels) pairs capping the sum of levels across all configurations of that building. A zero limit bans the building. State-region resource helpers produce limits in this form. construction_cost_cap None Maximum total construction points: the sum of building levels multiplied by each configuration's construction_cost. employment_cap None Maximum total employed population: the sum of building levels multiplied by per-level employment. arable_land_cap None Maximum total arable-land use. Each level in the model's agricultural, plantation, ranching, or subsistence land-use groups consumes one unit; other configurations consume zero. min_infrastructure None Minimum weighted total of building levels using the production-table infrastructure_usage_per_level column, with missing values treated as zero. It constrains that usage total; it does not subtract usage from infrastructure supplied by production methods. urbanization_per_center None Urbanization points required per level of building_urban_center. Enforces an equality: total building urbanization equals this value multiplied by total urban-center levels. For example, 100.0 ties each center level to 100 urbanization points.

docs.title: Example scenario
docs.text:
from vic3_analysis import NominalOptimizer, Scenario

scenario = Scenario(
    produce=(("automobiles", 100.0),),
    objective="automation",
    import_limit=0.0,
    era_cap=5,
    banned_pms=("pm_diesel_engines",),
)
state = NominalOptimizer(economy).solve(scenario)

docs.title: Problem inspection and solving
docs.text:
Use optimizer.compile(scenario) to inspect the resulting LinearProblem before solving it, or optimizer.solve_problem(problem) to solve an already compiled problem. Shared context and constraints are compiled by BaseOptimizer; Scenario remains configuration-only.

For endogenous national prices, use MarketOptimizer. It supports gdp and gdp_per_capita, requires import_limit=None, and treats imports, exports, and pop_needs as fixed market orders that affect prices rather than goods balance constraints. Its SLSQP solve is local and requires a bounded scenario. The model excludes shortages, MAPI and local prices, wealth feedback, endogenous demand, and economy-of-scale bonuses.

from vic3_analysis import MarketOptimizer, Scenario

scenario = Scenario(
    produce=(("automobiles", 100.0),),
    objective="gdp_per_capita",
    import_limit=None,
    exports=(("automobiles", 100.0),),
    employment_cap=1_000_000.0,
)
state = MarketOptimizer(economy).solve(scenario)

docs.title: State-region limits
docs.text:
from vic3_analysis import (
    StateRegionsParser,
    state_region_arable_land_limit,
    state_region_resource_limits,
)

regions = StateRegionsParser().to_dataframe()
keys = ("STATE_KANTO", "STATE_KANSAI")
limits = state_region_resource_limits(regions, keys)
land = state_region_arable_land_limit(regions, keys)

scenario = Scenario(
    objective="gdp",
    building_limits=tuple(limits.items()),
    arable_land_cap=land,
)

docs.title: Generate the tables

Run the comprehensive examples/parse.py script from the project root to generate all parsed game tables and the buy-package charts:

uv run python -m examples.parse

You can also run it directly with uv run examples/parse.py. Outputs write to artifacts/datasets/parsed/. The buy-package CSV is stored at artifacts/datasets/parsed/buy_packages/buy_packages.csv, with its linear and log-scale charts in the adjacent figures/ directory. These charts are views of the parsed dataset.

Initialize the pinned artifact submodule before running the examples:

git submodule update --init --recursive

Regenerate in dependency order: run examples/parse.py first, then examples/production_analysis.py, then the desired analysis scripts. Existing files at old artifact paths are not used as fallback inputs.

Generated data follows your installed game version

Regenerating a CSV may change many rows when the installed Victoria 3 version differs from the committed snapshot. Review those changes before replacing tracked data.

docs.title: Use individual parsers
docs.text:
Call individual parsers when you need tables in memory for a Python analysis. The package searches common Steam library locations on Windows, Linux, and macOS. If detection fails, pass game_dir="/path/to/Victoria 3/game" to the parser constructor or function.

For example, BuildingsParser exposes to_dataframe(), while goods() returns a DataFrame directly:

from vic3_analysis import BuildingsParser, goods

buildings_df = BuildingsParser().to_dataframe()
goods_df = goods()

print(buildings_df.head())
print(goods_df.head())

For other parsers and their parameters, see the parsing API reference.

docs.title: Build the production table
docs.text:
The production table remains a separate step using the generated CSVs:

uv run examples/production_analysis.py

production_table() iterates through every possible building and production method combination, then analyzes the resulting goods flows, employment, and other metrics. For further explanation of the columns, see the production-table dictionary.

The above script reads artifacts/datasets/parsed/ and writes artifacts/datasets/production/production_table.csv. You can also build the production table directly from the parsers:

from vic3_analysis import (
    BuildingsParser,
    PopTypesParser,
    ProductionMethodParser,
    goods,
    production_table,
    technology,
)

df_production = production_table(
    BuildingsParser().to_dataframe(),
    goods(),
    ProductionMethodParser().to_dataframe(),
    technology(),
    PopTypesParser().to_dataframe(),
)
df_production.to_csv("production_table.csv", index=False)

The technology and pop-types tables are optional enrichments. Without the technology table, production_table() keeps the raw unlocking_tech keys but omits era and unlocking_tech_localization. Without the pop-types table, it omits wage_normalized_employment and profit_per_wage_normalized_employment_nominal. For example, a base table needs only the first three inputs:

df_production = production_table(buildings_df, goods_df, production_methods_df)

To add wage-normalized metrics without technology enrichment, pass pop types by keyword:

df_production = production_table(
    buildings_df,
    goods_df,
    production_methods_df,
    df_pop_types=pop_types_df,
)

docs.title: Add localization
docs.text:
Localization is opt-in. Pass Victoria 3's internal language name to a parser to add a nullable localization column beside each identifier, while retaining the original script keys for joins and analysis:

from vic3_analysis import BuildingsParser, goods

goods_df = goods(language="english")
buildings_df = BuildingsParser().to_dataframe(language="english")

The localized values are the raw strings from the game files: references, formatting, icons, and localization functions are preserved. Missing entries are pd.NA; no fallback language is applied. Use localization("english") for the complete catalog, including related keys such as technology/building descriptions and lens-option suffixes.

production_table() propagates localization columns when its input tables contain them. Economy(language="english") applies the same option only to tables it parses internally; explicitly supplied DataFrames remain unchanged. Localization does not change the default no-language behavior.

See the parsing API for constructor parameters, return values, and exceptions.

docs.title: Supply-chain analysis
docs.text:
The supply-chain data dictionary defines every report column, its scope, units, formulas, and failure behavior.

SupplyChainAnalyzer runs one nominal optimization for one terminal good and returns an immutable result. The scenario must contain exactly one positive production target, and that target must match terminal_good.

from vic3_analysis import Economy, Scenario, SupplyChainAnalyzer

economy = Economy()
scenario = Scenario(
    name="automobiles",
    produce=(("automobiles", 1.0),),
    objective="automation",
)
result = SupplyChainAnalyzer(economy, scenario, "automobiles").run()

The result snapshots the compiled matrices, solved state, production metadata, and HiGHS diagnostics. Later changes to the economy or another optimizer do not change it.

docs.title: Inspect tables and graphs
docs.text:
headline = result.summary()
goods = result.goods()
processes = result.processes()
flows = result.flows()
workforce = result.workforce()
constraints = result.constraints()
bottlenecks = result.bottlenecks()
alternatives = result.alternatives("automobiles")
graph = result.graph()

Every table has a stable schema, including when it is empty. Process economics retain exact coproduct contributions. The API does not silently allocate a multi-output process's value to individual goods.

Two graph views are available:

  • realized is the default and contains active configurations upstream of the terminal good.
  • allowed contains technology choices not disabled by era, PM bans, building-group bans, or zero building limits. It is not a claim that every route is independently LP-feasible.

Both are cyclic bipartite NetworkX graphs: goods point to consuming production configurations, and configurations point to output goods. Cycles remain strongly connected components; they are never relabeled as raw-resource leaves. graph() returns a defensive copy.

docs.title: Why the graph uses processes
docs.text:
Normally we would say an Economy contains a set of buildings. However, since a building key can appear in several times with different production methods, we choose to rename it to processes.

This terminology follows the process/product distinction explained in Brightway's inventory documentation. Brightway is a Python life cycle assessment (LCA) framework whose inventory model separates transformations from the products they consume and supply. Here, production configurations are the transformations and Victoria 3 goods are the products. Brightway also uses activity in its API; its glossary shows that this term has broader usage than just production processes.

Consequently, process:<configuration-key> identifies a node, building remains its source metadata, and result.processes() reports configuration economics. The term does not mean an operating-system process.

The supply-chain design references compare this architecture with Brightway, PyPSA, Calliope, pymrio, and openLCA. They explain the shared ideas behind graphs, optimization, economic accounting, and explicit coproduct treatment, together with the limits of each comparison.

docs.title: Visualize the result
docs.text:
mermaid = result.to_mermaid()
network_figure = result.plot_network(metric="value")
contribution_figure = result.plot_contributions(metric="gdp", scope="chain")
balance_figure = result.plot_goods_balance()
constraint_figure = result.plot_constraints()

These methods return text or Matplotlib Figure objects and do not write files. Allowed-view diagrams retain active producers and otherwise show the top three producers per good by adjusted output rate.

docs.title: Sweep all producible goods
docs.text:
from vic3_analysis import Scenario, sweep_supply_chains

template = Scenario(
    name="era_3",
    objective="construction_cost",
    era_cap=3,
)
sweep = sweep_supply_chains(
    economy,
    template,
    target_value=100_000.0,
    keep_results=True,
)

summary = sweep.summary
failures = sweep.failures
automobiles = sweep.result_for("automobiles")

The sweep ignores a non-empty template produce basket and emits a UserWarning, because each target is derived from goods and target_value. By default, it follows economy.producible_goods order and targets an equal base-price value for each good. Infeasible or unbounded goods become failure rows and do not abort later runs. Version 1 executes sequentially.
